newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest bourse CEO quits to head rating agency.
newsitem.headline: Budapest bourse CEO quits to head rating agency.

text.p: Jozsef Rotyis, chief executive officer of the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE), announced on Friday he would step down from his post in the autumn to become head of Hungary's first credit rating agency, to be launched later this year.
The agency, Focus, will operate as a company with major banks, securities houses and other professional investors as shareholders, Rotyis said.
He said the new agency will fill a gap in the institutional system of the Hungarian capital markets.
"There is strong demand that a missing element of the capital market institutional infrastructure should help in the decisions of investors and securities issuers," Rotyis said in a statement.
The current market situation favours setting up such an agency, Rotyis said, adding there was increasing demand for bond issues, as interest rates and the inflation are declining.
Focus plans to enter into a strategic partnership with a leading international rating agency, Rotyis said without giving further details other than that negotiations were already underway.
Rotyis said Focus was unlikely to be the only new credit rating agency in Hungary.

"There are other attempts (to set up agencies), we think some of them will remain afoot," Rotyis said. "This is very good, because we don't want to see a situation in which they turn to us just because we are the only one."

Focus is being organised with the assistance of First Washington Associates Ltd under the auspices of the US Agency for International Development (USAID), in cooperation with the Hungarian Banking Association.
